title: New-evidence re-analysis case: referral program signup spike revisited with an independent source log

input.researchQuestion: Did the June referral program cause the signup spike?

datasets.description: Fictional monthly new-signup totals before and after the referral program launched in June.
Fictional server-side signup source-attribution log, pulled independently after the initial May-to-June finding, breaking the 500 new June signups down by referral tag and IP range.

expectations.text: If the referral program caused the spike, most of the 500 new June signups should carry a referral attribution tag in the source log.

hypotheses.text: The referral program caused the June signup spike.
A traffic anomaly unrelated to the referral program inflated the June signup count.

evidence.summary: Signups rose from 400 to 900 the month the referral program launched.
Only 80 of the 500 new June signups carry a referral attribution tag; the rest are unaccounted for by the referral program.
420 of the 500 new signups share a narrow IP range, independent of the referral program's own attribution tagging.

requiredLimitations: The source-attribution log was pulled after the initial finding and covers only June; it cannot rule out genuine referral-driven signups in later months.
A shared IP range is suggestive of automated signups but is not a definitive bot or fraud determination.
The original May-to-June comparison alone cannot separate the referral launch from the concurrent traffic anomaly.

requiredResearchGaps.need: A bot/fraud classification pass on the 420 suspicious signups (e.g. email verification rate, device fingerprint).
Daily signup counts around the referral launch date and the start of the suspicious traffic, to separate the two by timing.
Signup counts for a comparable period with the referral program active but without the traffic anomaly.

forbiddenClaims: 紹介プログラムが増加の原因である
the referral program drove the signup increase
不正アクセスであることが確認された

humanReview.notes: A passing report must not keep crediting the referral program once the independent source log contradicts it, and must not overclaim the suspicious-IP signups as confirmed fraud.
